title: El Niño and essential health services in India: HMIS state-month panel, code, results contract and aggregate data
description:
Code, every reported number and the aggregate data of a pre-specified state-month analysis of El Niño and the continuity of essential maternal, child and outpatient services in India (manuscript; citation to follow), from routine Health Management Information System (HMIS) reports for 34 state-level units, April 2012 to February 2020. Negative binomial mixed models relate antenatal care registration, third doses of a DPT-containing vaccine, institutional deliveries, outpatient attendance and reported childhood diarrhoea to the El Niño phase of the traditional Oceanic Niño Index (with a time random effect), to the interaction of El Niño with state monsoon sensitivity and to local heatwave days and rainfall deficit (year-month fixed effects), under verdict rules fixed in a results contract committed before any exposure model was fitted; with pre-specified minimum detectable effects, mediation by local climate, state heterogeneity, distributed lags, the Indian Ocean Dipole, an ENSO-index comparison (traditional ONI, RONI, Niño-3.4) and an out-of-sample forecast comparison.

Contents: the Python HMIS pipeline (download, parsing of three portal formats, indicator crosswalk, completeness flags, gates) with synthetic test fixtures; the R analysis; the results contract and its dated amendments; every reported number (results.json) with its traceability table; the derived state-month panel and model table (official state rows and district-completeness shares; no district-level values); aggregate outputs and figure data. Raw HMIS workbooks are not redistributed; the HMIS data carry the Government Open Data License – India attribution.
